Subject: Re: PrivCP IdP proxy + egress constraints — SCIM & RBAC mapping for Acme

Thanks Alicia — we'll run through these in the call. Quick responses in advance: 

- Metadata behind your IdP: we support both (1) pulling metadata from a customer-hosted endpoint over TLS and (2) uploading metadata directly to the private control plane during onboarding. If you cannot expose a public URL, uploading the metadata file (like the one you attached) is fully supported.
- SAML attributes: Redwood recommends an initial mapping using the standard "groups" assertion for RBAC and an optional "role" attribute for coarse-grained bindings. Karthik will follow up with a mapping table (attribute name -> scope -> PrivCP role).
- SCIM: our connector supports SCIM 2.0 push provisioning and PATCH for group membership. We prefer idempotent PATCH semantics (add/remove members) for large orgs.
- Egress: there are two patterns: (A) minimal egress — outbound to a narrow set of IPs we provide (region-specific), or (B) deploy a small IdP proxy inside your VPC that the control plane talks to via private peering. Pattern B avoids public egress for IdP metadata calls.

I'll put Karthik on thread to share the attribute/role mapping doc and a short checklist. Proposed time: Jan 31 09:30 PST — does that work?

Thanks,
Ava
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia@acmeanalytics.com>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: 2027-02-01T08:46:00-08:00
Subject: PrivCP attribute & RBAC mapping + SCIM behavior (details)

Alicia / Sam — following up with the technical details we committed to on the call. Summary + recommended config: 

1) SAML assertion mapping (recommended):
   - NameID: persistent, used to map to PrivCP user id.
   - urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User:externalId (if available): accepted but we rely primarily on NameID.
   - groups (SAML multi-valued): map to PrivCP group objects. We suggest a transform rule to prefix customer groups with "acme/" to avoid collisions.
   - custom attribute "privcp_role": optional, accepts "operator", "admin", "viewer" — when present, this will be used to short-circuit group-based role assignment.

2) RBAC model:
   - Primary: group -> role bindings (recommended for enterprise setups).
   - Secondary: privcp_role attribute for exceptions (short-lived admin access).
   - Group membership changes should be driven by SCIM patch operations; our connector processes PATCH/add/remove for group.members by value.

3) SCIM:
   - Modes supported: push (IdP -> PrivCP), pull (PrivCP polls IdP) — push is preferred for lower latency.
   - PATCH support: yes (we support RFC7644 PATCH semantics for group updates).
   - Bulk sync: we support full sync over the SCIM endpoint; for large orgs >25k users we recommend incremental patches with change tokens.

4) IdP metadata & certs:
   - You may upload metadata directly into the control plane or expose an HTTPS endpoint. If you upload, keep a copy in your Ceremonial Vault (we will record fingerprint as part of the onboarding manifest).
   - SAML signing certs should be RSA2048 or stronger; we also accept ECDSA certs for SAML2.

5) Network/egress patterns (detailed):
   - Pattern A (managed egress whitelist): PrivCP will need outbound TLS to our IdP metadata pull IPs: 35.202.112.0/24 (us-west), 34.120.200.0/24 (us-east) — we will provide final /32s during onboarding.
   - Pattern B (IdP proxy inside customer VPC): recommended for air-gapped customers. Architecture: your IdP and proxy in VPC -> private peering/Transit -> PrivCP control plane VPC endpoint. In this mode, no public egress from your network is required for metadata or SCIM calls.
   - MTLS recommendation: for extra protection we can enable mutual TLS between your proxy and our control plane endpoint (mutual certs rotated via your KMS).

6) Fallbacks & operational notes:
   - If SCIM push fails, the connector will queue up to 72 hours of changes (configurable) and retry with exponential backoff.
   - Role revocation: group removals propagate in <= 90s in normal load; for emergency revoke we recommend a short-lived emergency admin revocation webhook that our SRE team can trigger (requires SOC approval).

Attachments: privcp-scim-schema.csv (SCIM attributes we consume), saml-attribute-mapping.pdf (detailed mapping table).

Action items for Acme:
- Confirm whether you prefer Pattern A (whitelist) or Pattern B (proxy).
- If Pattern B, share preferred CIDR for proxy and the cert issuer.
- If Pattern A, we will provide final IP /32s and SNI names for TLS.

I'll be available on Feb 2 for any followups.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference
(attachment: privcp-scim-schema.csv, text/csv; attachment: saml-attribute-mapping.pdf, application/pdf)
